name: Excommunication
overview: Scripture teaches that excommunication is a serious church discipline exercised to maintain doctrinal purity and restore a repentant believer. Jesus grants the authority to bind and loose on earth with heavenly approval, emphasizing the church's responsibility in addressing sin within the community (Matthew 16:19). The process begins with private correction, escalating to involving the church if the offender refuses to repent, ultimately treating the unrepentant as an outsider (Matthew 18:15, 17). Paul further instructs believers to identify and avoid those who cause divisions and contradict sound doctrine, and to reject persistent heretics even after repeated admonition (Romans 16:17; Titus 3:10).
